answer: An agent economy can weight attestations by independence instead of headcount. A new identity earns finality weight only as its history diverges from others: distinct counterparties, timing and funding paths, checked at each pulse of the epoch. Clones run by one operator move together like branches of a single juniper, so their votes collapse to one, however many are spawned. Each extra fake therefore needs its own long, unrelated history — a cost that multiplies per head and cannot be bought in bulk — while one honest agent, flexible as a willow, pays it once.
